circuit/breaker/poles: reaches circuit.is_240v and stops there; the voltage attribute comes from the declared nominal voltage, or the tab count where none is declared, so no entity or attribute reads the field
circuit/connection/backed-up: whether the circuit stays powered off-grid; no entity reads it, and the shed priority select already shows how the panel treats the circuit
circuit/connection/count: no adapter maps it: it counts the physical units aggregated downstream (microinverters, packs), which nothing here models
circuit/connection/fed-by-device-id: the fed-by half of a circuit's connection record; the library reads only the feeds-* half, and no entity models what feeds a circuit
circuit/connection/fed-by-device-status: the link health of whatever feeds the circuit; the library reads only the feeds-* half of the record, and no entity models a circuit's feed
circuit/connection/fed-by-device-type: redundant: the id dereferences to the device's declared $type, which is how the library already resolves classes
circuit/connection/feeds-device-id: declared and not published on this panel, so the probe names a device that does not exist and dereferences to nothing. Where it is published it places a DER on its circuit
circuit/connection/feeds-device-status: declared and not published on this panel; a circuit's link status is read only for the device its feeds-device-id names, and no circuit names one here
circuit/connection/feeds-device-type: redundant: the library resolves a DER's class by dereferencing feeds-device-id against the tree's declared $type
circuit/connection/feeds-role: read into circuit.feeds_role, which nothing renders yet; reading a solar role as generation is pending
circuit/info/dedicated: whether the circuit serves one appliance; commissioning metadata with no Home Assistant counterpart, so not surfaced
circuit/info/locations: where the circuit's loads are in the home; descriptive commissioning metadata with no Home Assistant counterpart, so not surfaced
circuit/info/tags: free-form commissioning labels; descriptive metadata with no Home Assistant counterpart, so not surfaced
distribution-enclosure/info/address-line: site property: it says where the panel is installed, so the library never turns it into a reading
distribution-enclosure/info/country-code: site property: it says where the panel is installed, so the library never turns it into a reading
distribution-enclosure/info/latitude: site property: it says where the panel is installed, so the library never turns it into a reading
distribution-enclosure/info/locality: site property: it says where the panel is installed, so the library never turns it into a reading
distribution-enclosure/info/longitude: site property: it says where the panel is installed, so the library never turns it into a reading
distribution-enclosure/info/name: the site's own name, which says whose panel it is; deliberately not surfaced, and the panel device is named by its config entry
distribution-enclosure/info/region: site property: it says where the panel is installed, so the library never turns it into a reading
distribution-enclosure/info/utility-mete: site property: it identifies the installation's utility meter, so the library never turns it into a reading
distribution-enclosure/status/postal-cod: deliberate skip: no curated entity, because location has no Home Assistant value. It does surface as a disabled vendor reading through extension adoption, where the recorder cost is opt-in rather than imposed
distribution-enclosure/status/relay: the enclosure's own relay state; no entity or attribute reads it, and no control is offered for it
distribution-enclosure/status/time-zone: deliberate skip: no curated entity, because Home Assistant owns the time zone and a mismatch is a Repair rather than an entity. It does surface as a disabled vendor reading through extension adoption
lugs/connection/backed-up: whether the lugs' feed is backed up off-grid; topology no entity models
lugs/connection/count: no adapter maps it: it counts the physical units aggregated downstream (microinverters, packs), which nothing here models
lugs/connection/fed-by-device-id: declared and not published on this panel; where it is published it decides whether the lugs are the service entrance and links a battery or inverter ahead of them
lugs/connection/fed-by-device-status: declared and not published on this panel; link health is read only for a battery or inverter the lugs name, and these lugs name none
lugs/connection/fed-by-device-type: redundant: the id dereferences to the device's declared $type, which is how the library already resolves classes
lugs/connection/feeds-device-status: feedthrough link-health; the feeds-* half of the downstream lugs record is topology to consume, and no producer publishes it
lugs/connection/feeds-device-type: redundant: the id dereferences to the device's declared $type, which is how the library already resolves classes
lugs/connection/feeds-role: what the lugs feed; read nowhere, since the lugs' role is fixed by which lugs they are
lugs/connection/service-rating: the service's rating ahead of the lugs; no entity reads it, and the current monitor judges the mains by the breaker ahead of them
